title: Tagliavini fact-finding mission presents its report on the origins of the August 2008 war
body:
On 30 September 2009 Heidi Tagliavini, head of the Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on the Conflict in Georgia, presented the mission's report of about 1,200 pages to international diplomats in Brussels. The mission had been commissioned by the European Union.

The report concluded that Georgia's shelling of Tskhinvali on the night of 7-8 August 2008 began the large-scale armed conflict, but it placed the attack within a longer period of rising tensions. Tagliavini said it was Georgia that "triggered off the war" and that Georgia's stated legal justifications for the attack did not validly explain it.

The report also found fault with Russia. According to Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty it criticised the mass granting of Russian citizenship in Abkhazia and South Ossetia, the presence of non-peacekeeping Russian troops in South Ossetia before the war, disproportionate military action on Georgian territory, long-standing support for separatist authorities and the recognition of the two regions as independent states. It said Russian claims of Georgian ethnic cleansing or genocide against South Ossetians were unsubstantiated, but raised "serious question marks" about the Russian army's inaction while South Ossetian irregulars committed atrocities against Georgian civilians. The report acknowledged that it may not reflect full "absolute veracity", since investigators may not have had access to all information.
